explanation.summary: This tunnel between 10.10.1.220 and 10.10.2.220 was checked against 12 rules: 6 passed, 5 failed, 2 of them high severity, and the rest could not be judged from this capture. Post-quantum posture: classical (quantum-vulnerable key exchange).

points.text: RFC8247-DH-MUST (high): the tunnel agreed on a key-exchange group that the IPsec standard (RFC 8247) says must not or should not be used (seen: MODP-1024). Why it matters: these groups are too weak today. What to do: remove that group from both ends and use MODP-2048 or stronger, or an elliptic-curve group.

V-207193 (high): the key exchange uses a Diffie-Hellman group below what the US DoD requires (group 16 or higher) (seen: MODP-1024). Why it matters: a weaker key exchange is easier for a well-funded attacker to break later. What to do: configure a stronger group, such as ECP-384 or MODP-4096.

RFC8247-DH-OFFER (medium): one side still OFFERS key-exchange groups that RFC 8247 forbids, even if this tunnel did not pick one (seen: MODP-1024). Why it matters: any peer (or an attacker in the middle) that asks for the weak group can get it. What to do: delete the weak groups from that endpoint's proposal list.

V-207223 (medium): the handshake's integrity check is weaker than SHA-384 (seen: HMAC-SHA1-96). Why it matters: the integrity check is what stops tampering with the handshake. What to do: use a SHA-384 or SHA-512 based integrity setting.

DST-PQ-KE (informational): the key exchange is classical only, with no post-quantum part (seen: classical-only). Why it matters: traffic recorded today could be decrypted later by a large quantum computer. What to do: plan a move to a hybrid post-quantum key exchange (ML-KEM added to the classical one).
